title: Exterior algebra and exterior powers of a module
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $E$ an $R$-module. Let $\mathrm T(E)=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}E^{\otimes n}$ be the tensor algebra of $E$ over $R$ ($E^{\otimes0}=R$, $E^{\otimes1}=E$, multiplication by concatenation of pure tensors, tensor products of modules as in [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]). The *exterior algebra* $\wedge(E)=\wedge_R(E)$ is the quotient of $\mathrm T(E)$ by the two-sided ideal generated by the elements $x\otimes x$, $x\in E$; it is an associative $R$-algebra with unit $1$, its product is written $\wedge$, and $\iota:E=E^{\otimes1}\to\wedge(E)$, $v\mapsto v$, is $R$-linear with $v\wedge v=0$ (hence $v\wedge w=-w\wedge v$) for $v,w\in E$. For $n\ge0$ the *$n$-th exterior power* $\wedge^n_R(E)\subset\wedge(E)$ is the image of $E^{\otimes n}$, i.e. the $R$-submodule spanned by the products $v_1\wedge\dots\wedge v_n$ ($v_i\in E$; $\wedge^0_R(E)=R\cdot1$); the map $(v_1,\dots,v_n)\mapsto v_1\wedge\dots\wedge v_n$ is $R$-multilinear and alternating (zero when two $v_i$ are equal), $\wedge(E)=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}\wedge^n_R(E)$ as $R$-modules, and $\wedge^m_R(E)\wedge\wedge^n_R(E)\subset\wedge^{m+n}_R(E)$. One puts $\wedge^n_R(E)=0$ for $n<0$.
